I've opened a fix for this in #23018 — adds a `window-all-closed` handler to the Electron app so the `opencode-cli serve` sidecar gets killed when the window is closed on macOS.

Root cause: on macOS, closing the window doesn't quit Electron, so the existing `before-quit`/`will-quit` cleanup hooks never fire. The sidecar survives indefinitely.

Thanks for updating the issue! Everything looks good now — the feature request is clear, well-described, and follows the contributing guidelines. We appreciate you taking the time to improve it.

**Related issues:**
- #11189 requested `skills.search_paths` config but was closed without resolution
- #14240 covers the same concept for commands/agents

This issue is specifically about the **performance impact** of scanning multiple directories — 5+ seconds of startup time spent reading and deduplicating identical skills across `~/.claude/skills/`, `~/.agents/skills/`, and `~/.config/opencode/skills/`.

Even a minimal fix — like respecting `skills.paths` as an **override** (replace defaults when set) rather than an **additive** list — would solve the startup regression without needing a new config key.

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B also has similar needs to [preserve thinking](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B#preserve-thinking), example from the linked page:
```
from openai import OpenAI
# Configured by environment variables
client = OpenAI()

messages = [...]

chat_response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B",
    messages=messages,
    max_tokens=32768,
    temperature=0.7,
    top_p=0.8,
    presence_penalty=1.5,
    extra_body={
        "top_k": 20,
        "chat_template_kwargs": {"preserve_thinking": True},
    }, 
)
print("Chat response:", chat_response)
```
